newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street shares seen firm at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street shares seen firm at open.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open slightly higher on Monday, recovering from steep losses on Friday as the bond market showed early signs of stability ahead of this week's economic data.

"The bond market is up after a pretty big tumble after the last few days," Alfred Kugel, Stein Roe & Farnham senior investment strategist, said. "As it stabilizes, it could mean the end, short-term, of declines in the stock market."
The bond market, whose rising yields revived rate fears on Friday and sent stocks stumbling from recent highs, was up 5/32 to yield 6.62 percent.
The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index rose 2.25 points to 938.65.
But analysts said the inflation-wary bond market would remain wary ahead of a rash of economic data due later in the week which would offer clues into the pace of economic growth.
July retail sales data, due on Wednesday, and both the producer and consumer price indices would receive particular attention, they said.
